record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Consumer-resource-memory models with dynamic cognitive maps
record.original_question: Consider the two consumer-resource-memory systems where consumers satisfy ∂_t u = D1Δu − γ∇·(u∇q_g,R) + cβuv/(α+v) − du, the resource satisfies ∂_t v = D2Δv + rv(1 − v/K) − βuv/(α+v), and the memory map q evolves either by ∂_t q = bv − μq or by ∂_t q = buv − (μ + ξu)q. Under periodic boundary conditions in a bounded domain with a top-hat detection function, in what sense do time-dependent solutions exist, in what sense do spatially non-constant steady states exist, and what qualitative properties do those steady states have?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 21. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain, and consider the following coupled consumer–resource–memory PDE systems for unknowns $u(x,t)\ge 0$ (consumer density), $v(x,t)\ge 0$ (resource density) and $q(x,t)\ge 0$ (cognitive memory map), with positive constants $D_1,D_2,\gamma,c,\beta,\alpha,d,r,K,b,\mu,\xi$ and perception radius $R>0$.

Define the nonlocal "perceived memory" by the spatial convolution
$$q_{g,R}(x,t)=\int_{\Omega} g_R(x-y)\,q(y,t)\,dy,$$
where $g_R$ is the top-hat detection kernel
$$g_R(z)=\frac{\mathbf{1}_{\{|z|\le R\}}}{|B_R(0)|}.$$

The consumer and resource equations are
$$\partial_t u = D_1 \Delta u - \gamma\,\nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl(u\,\nabla q_{g,R}\bigr) + \frac{c\beta uv}{\alpha+v} - d u,$$
$$\partial_t v = D_2 \Delta v + r v\!\left(1-\frac{v}{K}\right) - \frac{\beta uv}{\alpha+v},$$
together with one of the two memory laws
$$\text{(M1)}\quad \partial_t q = b v - \mu q,\qquad \text{(M2)}\quad \partial_t q = b u v - (\mu + \xi u)\,q.$$
Periodic boundary conditions are imposed on $\partial\Omega$ for $u,v,q$, with non-negative initial data.

Address the following questions for each of the two systems (with (M1) and with (M2)):

(a) In what function-space sense (e.g. weak, mild, classical) do global-in-time solutions to the time-dependent problem exist, given that the kernel $g_R$ is discontinuous?

(b) In what sense do spatially non-constant stationary solutions $(u^*,v^*,q^*)$ exist (e.g. via bifurcation from constant equilibria, variational methods, degree theory)?

(c) What qualitative properties (positivity, regularity, stability, monotonicity, dependence on $R$, $\gamma$, and other parameters, pattern type) do these non-constant steady states possess?
artifact.status_search_result: Several recent works partially address this problem. Shen–Wang (J. Nonlinear Sci., 2024) and a 2025 J. Math. Anal. Appl. paper establish global existence, uniqueness, and stability of homogeneous steady states for cognitive consumer–resource models with nonlocal memory under periodic boundary conditions, including discontinuous top-hat kernels. Bifurcation and pattern-formation analyses (e.g., Nonlinear Dynamics 2024 with top-hat kernel; Ye–Wang SSRN 2025; SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2024) treat aspects of non-constant steady states. A complete answer covering both memory laws (M1) and (M2) and full qualitative classification of non-constant steady states does not yet appear settled.
